art.title: Birds
art.why: 'See the birds of the sky' (Matthew 6:26): many birds on and around a small tree, none of them storing anything.
No house on a rock (or the wise and foolish builders).

art.title: Agrippina and Germanicus
art.why: Two noble Romans in profile like a cameo: the Roman ideal of the hero and his family that Nietzsche admired. The spec's 'hero beside a humble saint' pair was not available; the Triumph of Camillus and Decius Mus were claimed first.
Saint Martin: El Greco's is used and both other versions are claimed (right-and-wrong, chivalry).

music.why: 'Forgive our foolish ways': a Quaker poet's hymn about the hills of Galilee and quiet obedience.
Law kept inwardly: music written for worship that was against the law of the land.
Martin Luther King's favourite hymn, sung at his funeral: the song of the man who lived enemy-love in public.
A hymn of creation's freshness each day: 'do not worry about tomorrow'.
A hymn for building on rock: trust in the one who made it.
'Have mercy on me': the humility Nietzsche despised, sung at its most beautiful.
Where love is, God is: the Sermon lived with grace.
